words: فِى بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These houses primarily mean worship places built at God's direct command: the Kaʿbah by Abraham and Ishmael and Bayt al-Maqdis by Solomon, with their branches included; idolatrous shrines are excluded as abodes of filth.
rows.anchor: their foremost connotations are the worship places that were built as a result of His direct command

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the faith parable names mosques, the discourse describes how believers live; it states the effect after its cause so faith is personified in lived conduct.
rows.anchor: This is like stating the effect after stating the cause so that a fact can be personified in real life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase for morning and evening means day and night, as in ordinary language.
rows.anchor: has the same meaning as that of “day and night” in our language.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun رجال intensifies praise: these are superb servants whom worldly things cannot distract from remembering God, whose pleasure they cherish most.
rows.anchor: is meant for extreme praise of such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tijārah means trade generally, while bayʿ conventionally means selling; the wording names a specific activity after the general term.
rows.anchor: conventionally means “to sell.” This is a mention of the specific after the general.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even highly profitable chances to sell do not distract these believers from God's remembrance; they conduct business without neglecting remembrance or their obligations.
rows.anchor: A businessman never loses the opportunity to sell his goods if the occasion arises; however, such are these servants of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakāh are the two basic religious duties and in reality encompass the whole religion.
rows.anchor: The prayer and zakāh are mentioned as two basic obligations of religion. In reality, they encompass the whole of religion

words: يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًۭا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of hearts and eyes turning over depicts Judgment Day's horrors, when people who lived heedlessly remain anxious and dismayed.
rows.anchor: portray the horrors of the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in verse 24:38 expresses consequence, not cause; Qur'an 28:8 and an Imruʾ al-Qays couplet support this usage, with the couplet's “on” carrying the consequential sense.
rows.anchor: Here too the on is meant to express the consequence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds, done from fear of the Hereafter and desire for God's pleasure, bring reward exceeding the deeds and further grace; they are forgiven beyond their imagining.
rows.anchor: for fear of the Hereafter and to earn the pleasure of God will be a source of a reward that surpasses their deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the believer parable, the disbeliever parable depicts their inner and outer selves; its darkness is equal to the believers' light.
rows.anchor: After mentioning the parable of belief and its bearers, now a parable of disbelief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' parable presents faith first as cause and deeds as effect; the disbelievers' parable reverses that order, showing their deeds first.
rows.anchor: In the parable of the believers, first the effect-producer (faith) is highlighted and then the effectee (deed).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is rooted deeply in human nature, with its blessed results visible in conduct; disbelief sprouts from filth, and its poisonous fruits are visible deeds without roots in human nature.
rows.anchor: faith is a very deep reality whose roots have penetrated deep into the nature of a human being

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers will find their deeds vanished like a mirage; instead they meet their Lord, who settles their account in the blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: they will encounter their Lord and He will settle their account in the blink of an eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's closing words picture the disbelievers' Hereafter misfortune and deprivation, with the complete sense continuing as ‘until when he arrives …’.
rows.anchor: Since the purpose of the parable is to explain their deprivation in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baḥr means deep sea; lujjī refers to the sea's deepest part and is described as its associated noun.
rows.anchor: refers to that part of the sea where the water is the deepest.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the parable of disbelievers' deeds, this verse gives a parable of their mental darkness: either disbelief in God or false belief leaves life in pitch darkness.
rows.anchor: The previous verse described a parable of the deeds of the disbelievers. This verse mentions a parable of their mental darkness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light comes only through faith in God; one not moved by God toward faith because of personal wretchedness cannot gain light and wanders in ever-deepening darkness until taking faith's path.
rows.anchor: A person who is not given the urge by God to accept faith – because of his own wretchedness – will never be able to obtain light.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the essence of belief and disbelief, the succeeding verses follow.
rows.anchor: Once the essence of belief and disbelief has been explained, the succeeding verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding imagery shifts discourse toward the mirage; the accusative pronoun gives due deference to the object being compared, the mirage.
rows.anchor: what deeds are compared to: mirage.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic kāfir or alladhīna kafarū does not denote those who deny God's existence: the addressees believed in God but associated partners, and polytheism is disbelief.
rows.anchor: These idolaters are called sometimes as disbelievers and sometimes as polytheists.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True belief requires affirming God with all His attributes and their implications; deeds of one who denies these have no Hereafter weight even if he considers them virtuous.
rows.anchor: believe in Him with all His attributes as well as all requisites of these attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending counters those who deem the Hereafter remote or doubt that countless deeds and words can be recorded: the negligent will see their account arrive instantly.
rows.anchor: the account of their deeds has come before them in the blink of an eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming verses first highlight God's attributes and majesty to show that He alone controls the universe and no one shares this power, so everyone should submit only to Him.
rows.anchor: only God is controlling this universe. No one else has any share in this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage then warns hypocrites that divided allegiance must end: they must obey God and His Messenger alone or face the promised rise of sincere servants and humiliation of their enemies.
rows.anchor: They should either devotedly show obedience only to God and His Prophet or remember that God will grant dominance to His sincere servants in this land

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 24:41 treats the same subject as 22:18: everything in the universe glorifies God; its observable form testifies to obedience while its inner form praises and exalts Him.
rows.anchor: Exactly the same subject as the one raised in this verse has been discussed in verse 18 of Sūrah al-Ḥajj.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans cannot understand created beings' language and gestures as they glorify and pray; the author also points to 17:44 on this.
rows.anchor: Human beings not being fully aware of their language and gestures though are not able to understand their glorification and prayers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation's practical demonstration calls humans to join in God's praise and worship Him alone; taking another way places one in discord with the rest of the world.
rows.anchor: through their practical demonstration invite human beings that they too join them in glorifying and exalting God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow God's path should not feel alone or outnumbered: every part of the universe accompanies them, despite a few ingrates choosing otherwise.
rows.anchor: The person who treads this path is never alone. This path is replete with caravans. Every entity of this universe is his fellow-passenger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds are singled out glorifying God in flight; their outstretched wings portray prostration, while other passages refer to their chanting and singing.
rows.anchor: At some other instances, their chanting and singing is referred to. Here their outstretched wings portray their prostration before God.
